When the departure is superseded, cancelled or its navigator closes, the guard's token disposes the
subscription and the guard returns at once. ReactiveUI lets a running .NET handler finish; a Runic web View's handler receives an aborted

The departure fails closed: when no handler answers, ReactiveUI's

The question is asked in the guard, outside model turns, on the thread the guard runs on: the dispatcher for a WPF navigator, the thread pool otherwise.

A Runic web View's handler answers a departure that its own window starts: a bridged command of any View in that window, such as the page's Close or the shell's Back, asks the presentation mounted by the same browser connection; a guarded window close asks the window's one presentation with a mounted handler. A departure that .NET code starts outside both, such as a timer's navigation, reaches only .NET handlers. Handlers run latest first, as in ReactiveUI: one registered after the View attached, such as a WPF View's
handler, answers before the web View, and a fallback registered in the ViewModel's constructor answers only when no View does.
